source: Minchat Shai on Gen 16:5 (the Masorah; Masekhet Soferim 6 — the ten dotted places)
claim_en: THE DOTTED YOD — one of the Torah's TEN DOTTED PLACES (puncta, the scribal dots the schools expound): a dot stands OVER the last yod of וביניך ('and between YOU,' Sarai's judge-plea). SNAPSHOT CARRIES THE DOT — the upper-dot mark sits on the yod in the codex's own stream: the dotted-letters layer, long assumed invisible to the instrument, is INSTRUMENTED. First dotted place the program has reached; the machine's own boldest verse (the first human demand on God) wears it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 16:5 (the Hilleli; the Toledot Masorah: 'all defective except one')
claim_en: DISCREPANCY OBSERVATION — the plene ביניך: the Masorah rules every 'between-you' defective EXCEPT this one (16:5, with its two yods). SNAPSHOT: 16:5 plene as ruled — but 13:8's peace-plea ('between me and you,' Abram to Lot) is plene BESIDES, against the count (all nine others defective). One more than the law, kin to gen_30's eleven-that-are-eighteen; the DOT sits only on 16:5's yod (13:8's probed dotless). Filed, not merged.

אל ראי ('a God of SEEING' — the machine's own El-ladder token and registry write): the resh carries HATAF QAMATZ (the compound o-vowel) — the Masorah marks the pointing UNIQUE; SNAPSHOT points it exactly so. The Torah hapax the machine holds gets its one-of-a-kind vowel attested.

אחרי ראי ('AFTER the One who sees me') — the aleph in HIRIQ (the i-vowel), as ruled; SNAPSHOT exact. The two seeing-words of the naming verse carry two different vowel-shapes — the hapax pair pointed apart.

וקראת ('and you shall CALL...') — the Torah's consonantal census: four (16:11 Ishmael's naming-decree; 17:19 Isaac's; Deut 20:10 the peace-call; Deut 31:29 the evil that will BEFALL) — and the Masorah's four-member list takes the SHORT-POINTED pair (16:11, Deut 31:29 — probed: both end bare tav) and adds Isaiah's two: 'call his name IMMANU-EL' (7:14) and 'call your walls SALVATION' (60:18; edges): 'by Ishmael's calling came the evil; by Immanuel's calling, salvation' (Kitzur).

עניך ('your AFFLICTION' — 'for YHWH has heard your affliction'): written with ONE yod only, per the Ramah. SNAPSHOT: one yod — the affliction-word of the decree-chain (15:13 → 16:6 → 16:9 → 16:11, the machine's landed career) written lean at the hearing.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 16:5 (the Ramah: 'and so the whole Torah')
claim_en: בחיקך ('in your BOSOM,' Sarai's grievance): yod after the chet, none after the qof — the Ramah's rule for the word Torah-wide. SNAPSHOT exact at the grievance-verse where Sarai speaks the receipt-grammar (natati).

חמסי ('my WRONG') — ONE Torah token (16:5): the flood-word turned household grievance (the machine's chamas census) exists in first-person exactly once; the Masorah's pair: 'my violence and my flesh upon BABYLON, says the DWELLER OF ZION' (Jer 51:35; edge) — the Kitzur: Sarah likened to Zion, both barren, both wronged.

הרתה ('she had CONCEIVED') — exactly twice in the Torah, BOTH in this span (16:4, 16:5): the doubled conception-word is the Kitzur's hint for the tradition's reading (the evil eye entered, she miscarried and conceived again — Rashi's reading, named).

ולה ('and SHE had...') — ONE Torah token (16:1, 'and she had an Egyptian maid'); the Masorah's four run through the two-edged dagger (Judg 3:16), Eli's peace-word to Chanah (I Sam 1:17), and Daniel's four-winged beast (Dan 7:6) — edges; the Kitzur's Hagar-arc reading (her return as Keturah) rides named-only.

ושרי אשת ('and Sarai, WIFE of...') — the name-form's adjacency stands once in the Torah (16:1, the chapter's opening); the Masorah pairs it with 'and my princes in Issachar with DEBORAH' (Judg 5:15; edge): 'she was as important as the mothers.'

ברחת ('I am FLEEING') — ONE Torah token (16:8, Hagar's answer); the Masorah's pair: 'the whole city FLEEING from the horseman and the bow-shooter' (Jer 4:29; edge) — the Kitzur: the bow-shooter is Ishmael himself (21:20's roveh qashat), the flight repaid.

עין המים ('the SPRING of water') — the adjacency's Torah census: three stands (16:7 the angel finds Hagar; 24:13 the servant stationed; 24:43 the servant retelling his station — the retell doubling the phrase); the Kitzur's pair (16:7 with 24:13): 'it is good to pray at the water' — prayer likened to water poured (edges ride the reading).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 16:3 (most manuscript books)
claim_en: ותקח שרי אשת־אברם ('and Sarai, Abram's wife, TOOK') — no paseq (separator bar) after Sarai, and maqqef joining אשת to אברם, as in most manuscripts. SNAPSHOT: the maqqef stands — the wife-word bound to the husband's name in the verse where she gives the maid.
ותאמר ('and she said' — Hagar's answer): with ZAQEF GADOL (the great upright accent), as in the precise books. SNAPSHOT carries it — the runaway's answer stands under the big pause.

source: Tosefta Yevamot 8:4; Yevamot 64a:5; Bereshit Rabbah 45:3; Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 6:6:3; Mishnah Yevamot 6:6
claim_en: THE TEN-YEARS LAW IS DERIVED FROM OUR 16:3 AT FOUR SEATS - AND THE TRADITION GRADES ITS OWN DERIVATION AS WEAK. The Mishnah rules that a man who has waited ten years without children must act, and the Tanna's stated reason is this verse's own ten years in the land of Canaan, from which the rider follows that years spent outside the Land do not count, with further exclusions for sickness and imprisonment. But the Tosefta records the derivation's epistemic grade openly: 'NO PROOF, BUT A HINT' - and the Babylonian seat repeats it. A live obligation resting on a source the tradition itself marks as suggestive rather than probative.

check.note: A binding rule derived from this verse at four seats, with the tradition explicitly grading its own derivation as a hint rather than a proof.

claim_en: A RULE OF JUDICIAL RECOURSE IS DERIVED FROM OUR 16:5 AND THEN NARROWED. R. Chanan holds that whoever passes judgment on another to Heaven is punished first, with this verse's 'let the Lord judge between me and you' the proof and the later death the sequel. The Babylonian seat then adds the limiting clause the earlier statement lacked: only where earthly recourse exists. A rule stated broadly at one seat and refined at another, both carried.

check.note: A rule derived from this verse and then explicitly limited at a second seat, the refinement recorded rather than merged.

source: Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Vayehi Beshalach 5:4
claim_en: A RULE ABOUT THE MACHINE'S OWN NAME-TOKENS IS STATED WITH OUR VERSES AS THE TYPE-CASES. R. Natan states the rule to R. Shimon ben Yochai: wherever the text says 'the angel of the LORD' one thing is meant, and where it says 'angel of ELOHIM' JUDGMENT is meant, since that name everywhere denotes a judge. Our 16:7 and 16:9 are the type-cases of the first form. The divine-name distinction the unit records mechanically is here a named interpretive rule with this unit supplying its exemplars.

check.note: A rule about which divine name marks which mode, with this unit's tokens named as the type-cases.

claim_en: THE NAME COINED AT OUR 16:13 BECOMES A WORKING BLESSING FORMULA. The divine name given here is carried into live usage as a blessing - the one who SEES AND IS NOT SEEN - cited with a named precedent. The name is separately expounded as 'You who see the wretchedness of the wretched', with a seeing-hierarchy claim attached: the maidservant saw what her mistress did not. A name minted inside this unit and still in liturgical use.

check.note: A divine name coined in this unit and carried into standing liturgical usage.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 45:7; Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:6:10; Bereshit Rabbah 45:8
claim_en: TWO CENSUSES ARE COUNTED OFF THIS UNIT'S REPETITIONS, AND BOTH ARE DISPUTED. The number of angels is counted from the verses' own repeated verbs: FIVE on the count of the speech-verbs, FOUR on the count of the messenger-nouns - a numeric dispute read directly off our ink. And the census of those named before birth carries our Ishmael as a disputed member: 'some say also Ishmael, among the nations' at one seat, a full member at another. Two counts, both taken from this unit, both recorded with their variance.

check.note: Two censuses computed from this unit's own repeated tokens, each disputed, both carried per credit guard 3.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 45:6; Bereshit Rabbah 71:7; Bava Kamma 92b:5
claim_en: TWO LAWS ARE PLEADED INSIDE THE SCENE, AND THE SCENE ITSELF BECOMES PRECEDENT. Against the harsh treatment two statutes are cited within the narrative - the captive woman who may not be enslaved because she was afflicted, and the bondswoman who may not be sold in betrayal - so the episode is argued as a legal case in its own terms. The episode is then invoked as PRECEDENT by Rachel, who introduces her rival on the strength of it. And a standing proverb is sourced here: 'if your friend calls you a donkey, prepare a saddle', from the exchange in which the angel says 'maidservant of Sarai' and she answers 'my mistress Sarai'.

check.note: Statutes pleaded inside the narrative, the episode then cited as precedent by a later character, and a proverb sourced to its dialogue.

claim_en: THE RESTART CLAUSE OF THE TEN-YEARS LAW, SUPPLIED BY THE CASE SHELF. The ten-years rule is seated at G32-16 with its riders and its self-graded source. The Mishnah adds a clock rule the machine did not hold: a MISCARRIAGE RESTARTS the ten-year count - the years are counted from the miscarriage, not the marriage. Entered through the Step 9 pilot exam (finding F-002, owner: 'seat F-001 through F-003').

check.note: A counting rule on an obligation's clock; case-shelf only, no ink claim.

claim_en: THE INVOKER PUNISHED FIRST. Handing a fellow to Heaven's judgment punishes the invoker first — Sarai's cry answered at Sarah's eulogy, with the earthly-recourse condition. Filed F-194, auto-seated (round 41, the kindness block).
